title: Why does STM32MP257F-DK not having EMI-filters on RX lines for USB 3.0?
content:
Why does STM32MP257F-DK not having EMI-filters on RX lines for USB 3.0?

Can it be like a common standard that the transmitter TX should always have:

  • AC capacitors
  • ESD protection
  • EMI-filtering

And the RX does not need anything of those, because it’s assuming that their transmitter already having these implemented?

This picture is from mb1605-mp257f-c01-schematic.pdf
categoryName: STM32 MPUs Products and hardware related

scraped_replies.html:
Hi ​@Windows 

Checking USB3 standard in  USB 3.2 Revision 1.1 - June 2022 | USB-IF, section 6.8.3 Receiver Electrical Parameters

On RX, it seems optional.

​@FBL 

 

Thank you so much. Yes, the RX lines are optional for AC capacitors.

But why did ST not implement EMI filter for RX lines as well?  Just wondering.

Hi ​@Windows 

 

Probably multiple explanations (guess):

  • There is no product related emission on RX lines, so no need of EMI filter to fulfill product standards (FCC or similar).
  • There is already ESD protection inside FUSB340 switch RX
  • The serie capacitor on TX might need to be protected from ESD (I’m not sure about that)

 

Regards.

Thank you ​@PatrickF 

 

Yes. The FUSB340 have internal 2kV ESD protection. But that’s is only for packaging. 

 

According to the getting started manual for MP2, it recommends to use EMI filtering on both RX and TX.
